next.title: The Underwriting Desk is next.
next.body: The Underwriting Desk is in development and follows the same governance model as the Placement Desk: scoped authority, a complete record of every action, and a named person accountable for its work.

entry.title: The desk meets the work where it already is.

items.title: Forwarded by a producer
items.body: A submission or a renewal request forwarded to the desk, the way you would hand it to a colleague.

items.title: The desk’s own inbox
items.body: Renewals, carrier correspondence and client documents arriving at an address on your domain.

items.title: From your systems
items.body: An AMS event, a renewal date, or another trigger you define.

scope.eyebrow: How much the desk takes on
scope.title: The level of responsibility follows the business.

tiers.title: Toward near-zero-touch placement
tiers.body: Where the business is programmatic, the desk can increasingly carry placement through to returned quotes, with human review at the points your controls set.

tiers.title: The work around the decision
tiers.body: The desk gathers and validates information, prepares submissions, identifies markets, coordinates carrier interaction and advances the quoting process. Your professionals stay on strategy, negotiation and judgment.

company.body: We started with placement because it is where skilled work, execution burden and growth meet. The model extends from there.

security.body: Governance is not a layer added after the desk works. It is how the desk is allowed to work at all.

human.title: The line between execution and judgment is drawn on purpose.
items: Approval at every review point you define

careers.body: We hire people who know insurance deeply, people who build AI systems that do real work, and people who can do both.

platform.body: You do not assemble those controls yourself. You receive a desk that is already allowed to work this way, so it can be deployed into a brokerage rather than demonstrated to one.

items.title: Governed
items.body: Every action runs under a defined scope of authority that names what the desk may do, on which accounts and channels, and for how long. That authority expires and can be withdrawn. Accountability attaches to a named person.

items.title: Bounded
items.body: The desk follows playbooks that capture how your business does the work: the steps, the standards, the exceptions, and where a person must be asked. You are not handed an agent builder.

items.title: Auditable
items.body: Every consequential action is written to an append-only record with attribution, so a result can be reconstructed exactly as it happened.

architecture.title: Between the request and the system of record.
architecture.note: Integrations are configured per deployment. Common targets include Applied Epic, AMS360, Sagitta, ImageRight, SharePoint, Outlook and Teams.

carrier-channels.body: Your producers should not have to know which carrier answers by which channel. The desk knows, and works all three in parallel.

horizon.title: Placement is the first desk.
horizon.body: The same model extends to other defined insurance work as AI becomes capable of owning more of it. Our ambition is to help insurance businesses organize work around what people and AI are each best equipped to do.

title: Submissions in.
Quotes out, ready for review.
underwritingDesk.lead: The Underwriting Desk is the Placement Desk seen from the other side of the submission. Risks come in from brokers, the workforce is designed to carry each one through intake, appetite, rating and quoting, and a finished quote comes back to your underwriters for final review.
underwritingDesk.body: Underwriters spend much of their day on work that happens before the decision. The desk is built to take on that work, through to a quote, and hand the decision back.

entry.title: The desk meets the submission where it lands.

items.title: Broker email
items.body: Submissions and supplementals arriving at an underwriting inbox, in whatever shape the broker sends them.

items.title: Portal and API intake
items.body: Applications submitted through your portal or received through an API or comparative rater.

items.title: Your systems
items.body: A new submission in your policy administration or workbench system, or another trigger you define.

steps.title: Intake and structure
steps.body: The submission read as it arrives, with the application, schedules and loss runs structured into your data model.

steps.title: Appetite and guidelines
steps.body: Every risk checked against your appetite and underwriting guidelines, with out-of-appetite submissions declined or referred by your rules.

steps.title: Complete the file
steps.body: Missing information identified and requested from the broker, the thread worked until the file is complete, and third-party data pulled in where you use it.

steps.title: Rate
steps.body: The risk rated in your rating engine or by your rating rules, with the inputs and the derivation recorded.

steps.title: Quote
steps.body: Terms, conditions and pricing assembled into a quote to your standards, ready for the underwriter to review rather than to build.

steps.title: Return for review
steps.body: The quote, the file behind it and the record of how it was produced, returned to the underwriter for the final decision and release to the broker.

scope.eyebrow: How much the desk takes on
scope.title: The same model as placement, tuned to your book.

tiers.title: Quote-ready with a light review
tiers.body: Where risks fit clean guidelines, the desk is designed to carry a submission through to a quote, with the underwriter’s review at the points your controls define.

tiers.title: The file prepared, the judgment yours
tiers.body: Where a risk needs an underwriter’s judgment, the desk completes and structures the file, applies your guidelines, and presents the questions that remain. Your underwriters price and decide.

human.title: The desk quotes. Your underwriters decide.
items: Final review and release of every quote

cta.title: Talk to us about underwriting capacity.
cta.body: Tell us how submissions reach your underwriters today, how they are rated and quoted, and where the queue builds up. We will show you what the desk would take on.

columns.line: A producer forwards a submission, a renewal lands in the desk’s own inbox, or an AMS event.
Gathers the account, checks appetite and works the markets through portals, APIs and email.
Quotes, market results and a record of the work come back for review. The Desk handles multiple accounts in parallel using the same placement process.
